title: One teacher or a whole hall?

segments.text: One clever teacher, or a whole school hall? Which works faster?
Nvidia's famous chips are called GPUs, graphics processing units. They were first made to draw video games.
An ordinary computer brain, a CPU, is like one very clever teacher, solving sums one after another. A GPU is like a whole school hall of pupils, each solving one small sum, all at the same time.
And it turns out AI learns in a similar way: by doing billions and billions of small multiplications. So the chip built for games became the chip that helps teach AI.
Which finishes first: one friend with twenty sums, or twenty friends with one sum each?
